headline: Solvable: after applying the documented round-down rule and the WeWork/ThredUp exceptions, exactly two transactions are wrong, matching the gold. Only the rounding document is missing from the required list.

issues.summary: The rounding rule that decides which rows count as errors lives in doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007, which is not listed in required_documents. The agent can still find it with KB search or grep in the default alltools configuration.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
issues.why_it_matters: Under a retrieval configuration that only shows required_documents (golden_retrieval / required_docs prompt), the agent never sees the rounding rule, so whether a row counts as a 1-point error depends on whichever convention the agent assumes.

solution_check: Recomputed all 17 transactions for d2e5bc4124. Rules: Business Bronze 1%, WeWork 0% (doc _003); EcoCard 5x Green except the doc_ecocard_004 exclusions (ThredUp -> 1x), Tesla Supercharger is a certified network so 5x; floor. Floor gives exactly the 2 gold rows: ccbb94 (Chipotle $369.55 Bronze -> 369, stored 184) and 5b30a5 (Everlane $270.42 Green -> 1352, stored 270). Round-half-up adds 6 one-point false positives (ThredUp 50/51, HBO Max 142/143, Spotify 439/440, Tesla 240/241, Patagonia 805/806, DTE 282/283). The gold replay matches itself.
prior_note: The prior Major assumed floor rounding was undocumented. Doc _007 documents it, so only the Minor required_documents omission remains.
notes: The customer is told to accept explanations about coworking spaces and thrift stores, which matches WeWork at 0 points and ThredUp at 1x. No relaxed comparison in the verified scorer applies.
